```{r load-results}
#| code-summary: "Load cached pipeline outputs (no network, no model calls)"
facts      <- compute_facts(grants)
fact_val   <- function(label) facts$computed[facts$fact == label]
enrich     <- readRDS(file.path(DIR_PROCESSED, "grantsgov_enrichment.rds"))
alignment  <- readRDS(file.path(DIR_PROCESSED, "alignment.rds"))
labels_path <- file.path(DIR_PROCESSED, "llm_labels.rds")
labels     <- if (file.exists(labels_path)) readRDS(labels_path) else NULL
labels_ok  <- !is.null(labels) && sum(labels$labeled) > 0
payload    <- jsonlite::fromJSON(PAYLOAD_JSON, simplifyVector = FALSE)
opps       <- payload$opportunities
titles     <- select(grants, opportunity_number, opportunity_title, agency_code)

# The tier engine is src/tool/tiering.js; the notebook runs that same file through V8.
opening <- run_tiering_js(opps, payload$capabilities$profiles, payload$config$opening) |>
  left_join(titles, by = "opportunity_number")
tier_n  <- function(k) sum(opening$placement == "pile" & opening$tier == k)

handlabels <- load_handlabels()
validation <- if (labels_ok && !is.null(handlabels)) validate_labels(labels, handlabels) else NULL

cutoff_date <- FACT_REF_DATE + FACT_RUNWAY_DAYS
open_state  <- grants |> filter(status_group == "Posted", state_eligible, !is.na(close_date), close_date >= cutoff_date)
state_rows  <- grants |> filter(state_eligible)
windows     <- grants |> filter(status_group == "Posted", !is.na(application_window_days),
                                application_window_days >= 0, application_window_days <= WINDOW_MAX_DAYS)
implied     <- grants |> filter(!is.na(implied_award_usd))
closed_since <- sum(enrich$status$status_now %in% c("closed", "archived") &
                      grants$status_group[match(enrich$status$opportunity_number, grants$opportunity_number)] == "Posted", na.rm = TRUE)
nofo_n      <- sum(!is.na(enrich$nofo$nofo_text))
cand_n      <- nrow(enrich$nofo)
```

# 1. Executive summary

```{r kpis}
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "KPI cards"
kpi <- function(label, value, note, cls = "") {
  sprintf('<div class="kpi-card %s"><div class="kpi-label">%s</div><div class="kpi-value">%s</div><div class="kpi-note">%s</div></div>',
          cls, label, value, note)
}
cat('<div class="kpi-grid">',
    kpi("Opportunities in the file", n_fmt(nrow(grants)), paste("Grants.gov export pulled", format(PULL_DATE, "%b %d, %Y"))),
    kpi("Open and state-eligible", n_fmt(nrow(open_state)), paste("closing on or after", format(cutoff_date, "%b %d"))),
    kpi("Of those, NIH research", pct_fmt(mean(open_state$is_nih)), paste(n_fmt(sum(open_state$is_nih)), "need a university investigator"), "danger"),
    kpi("Writer can act today", tier_n(1), "Tier 1 in the opening scenario", "t1"),
    kpi("Needs supervisor", tier_n(2), "Tier 2", "t2"),
    kpi("Needs secretary or legislature", tier_n(3), "Tier 3", "t3"),
    '</div>')
```

A state agency grant writer does not need help *finding* federal opportunities; they need to
know which ones they can *act on*. We built a tool that sorts every relevant opportunity into
three piles by whose signature it requires: the writer's, a supervisor's, or the secretary's or
legislature's. The sorting comes from written rules that compare each opportunity's
requirements (match, capabilities, staff, subrecipients, construction, designations) against
a sourced profile of what the agency actually controls. Every opportunity carries the reason
it landed where it did, and every one of the `r n_fmt(nrow(grants))` is accounted for: research
awards sit in a fourth, partner-led pile, and everything outside the writer's scope is listed with
its reason. Within each pile, the writer can rank by an impact score whose weights they set.

The data explain why this matters. Of `r n_fmt(nrow(open_state))` open opportunities that list
state governments as eligible, `r n_fmt(sum(open_state$is_nih))` are NIH research awards. Being
"eligible" rarely means being the intended applicant: `r n_fmt(nrow(state_rows))` rows list
state governments, but only `r fact_val("Of those, state-government-only")` are restricted to
them. The median application window is `r median(windows$application_window_days)` days, and
`r pct_fmt(mean(windows$application_window_days <= 30), 1)` of windows are 30 days or shorter.

::: {.read-me}

Section 4 lists every dataset and where it is charted.</p>
<p><span class="lbl">Tiers</span><span style="color:#2a78d6;font-weight:700">Tier 1</span> the writer can act · <span style="color:#eb6834;font-weight:700">Tier 2</span> needs a supervisor or division · <span style="color:#1baf7a;font-weight:700">Tier 3</span> needs the secretary or legislature · <span style="color:#77756f;font-weight:700">Tier 4</span> research a partner would lead.</p>
:::

# 2. The user and what "good" means

We interviewed someone who writes grants. Their input reframed the project, and we checked it
against published sources before building on it.

**Our user** is a mid-level employee inside NC DHHS who writes and assembles federal
applications. Not leadership, not an analyst. They review roughly a hundred postings a week,
spend weeks on each application, and **cannot commit matching funds without a supervisor.**

**Five criteria, stated before any data, drive every step of the workflow:**

1. **We can actually be the applicant.** Not a research grant that needs a university principal investigator.
2. **We have the capabilities it requires,** or know which partner we would need. Needing housing when the agency does not control housing is a partnership problem, which is a calendar problem.
3. **There is enough runway.** The bottleneck is internal sign-off, not writing.
4. **The award justifies the staff weeks.** An application costs about the same effort at $200K as at $5M.
5. **The match is survivable** at the writer's level of authority.

**Why sort by authority.** Three published sources support the framing:

- Maryland's state grants office sorts go/no-go questions into deal-breakers (eligibility, core
  capabilities, deadline, award amount), fit, and strategy (readiness, impact, competitiveness)
  ([Maryland Governor's Grants Office, *Go or No-Go*](https://grants.maryland.gov/SiteAssets/Pages/Conference/Go%20or%20No-Go%20A%20Guide%20to%20Deciding%20Which%20Federal%20Grants%20are%20right%20for%20you.pdf)).
- Standard federal evaluation criteria score "Overall Qualifications of Applicants": whether the
  applicant has the facilities and administrative resources to do the work. Capacity is on the
  scoresheet ([NOAA evaluation criteria](https://www.corporateservices.noaa.gov/grantsonline/Documents/FFO_Help_Pages/FFO_Help_Evaluation_Criteria.htm);
  [OJP application guide](https://www.ojp.gov/funding/apply/ojp-grant-application-resource-guide)).
- Under 2 CFR 200.306 the non-federal match generally cannot come from other federal funds, so a
  match requirement needs someone with authority over state dollars
  ([2 CFR 200.306](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/subtitle-A/chapter-II/part-200/subpart-D/section-200.306)).

| Tier | Label | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Writer can act | Start today on their own authority |
| 2 | Needs supervisor or division | Match approval, new staff, or a partner agency |
| 3 | Needs secretary or legislature | Appropriation, capital project, statutory designation |

# 3. How we built this

The project changed direction once, and the model and data were corrected several times along the
way. This section records that path, because the corrections are part of why the results can be
trusted.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart LR
  A["Grants.gov export<br/>1,662 opportunities"] --> B["Clean and verify<br/>24 facts checked"]
  B --> C["Grants.gov API<br/>current status +<br/>full announcements"]
  C --> D["Local AI labeler<br/>requirements, domain,<br/>plan alignment"]
  P["DHHS and DMVA<br/>strategic plans"] --> D
  K["Capability profiles<br/>(hand-built, sourced)"] --> T
  D --> T["Tier rules<br/>tiering.js"]
  T --> U["Interactive tool<br/>+ this notebook"]
  H["60 blind<br/>hand labels"] -.validates.-> D
```

| Step | What we did | What changed as a result |
|---|---|---|
| Interview | Talked with a grant writer about how go / no-go decisions are really made | The output became piles sorted by whose signature is needed, not a ranked list |
| Verify the data | Computed `r nrow(facts)` facts about the file before building anything; the pipeline must reproduce each | One fact was wrong in our own notes (match percentages appear in 6 rows, not 1) and was corrected after checking all six by hand |
| Choose the plans | Used the strategic plans the competition provides (DHHS 2023-2025, DMVA 2025-2029), turned into tables with page numbers | Every plan row is re-checked against its PDF page on each render |
| Build the capability model | Hand-built 14 capabilities per agency with a control level and a source | Two sources did not support their claim and were replaced; one level was changed (DMVA data systems to partner) |
| Label with a local model | Prompt v2 labeled the first 118 candidates | Review showed it called most grants aligned with DHHS, including international and wildfire programs |
| Tighten the prompt | Prompt v3 made the definitions strict and was tested on known cases | It over-corrected (it rejected Title X); v3.1 fixed that and was checked on 16 development cases before the full run |
| Validate | The team labeled 60 opportunities without seeing the model's answers | Hard facts agree over 90% of the time; judgment calls 45-67% (section 12) |
| Review research items | The team read 27 research awards flagged as closely aligned | They recommended a separate research tier, which became Tier 4 |
| Build the tool | Rules in one JavaScript file, tested on every build, all 1,662 opportunities accounted for | The notebook runs the same rules, so the two can never disagree |
| Show who is reached | Added county, rural / urban and congressional-district counts for each population an opportunity serves | Leadership can see which communities an opportunity reaches, labeled as where people live, not where money goes |

# 4. Data provenance and data dictionary

| Source | What we used | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Grants.gov export `r basename(GRANTS_CSV)` | `r n_fmt(nrow(grants))` opportunities, `r ncol(grants_raw)` columns | Supplied by the competition; pulled `r format(PULL_DATE)` |
| Grants.gov public API | Current status for every opportunity; full announcements for `r n_fmt(nofo_n)` of `r n_fmt(cand_n)` candidates | Free, no key; cached with access dates |
| NC DHHS Strategic Plan 2023-2025 | Goals, objectives, strategies, priority questions (`r nrow(load_priorities() |> filter(agency == "DHHS"))` rows) | [OSBM agency plans](https://www.osbm.nc.gov/strategic-plan-ncdhhs/open), the competition's source |
| NC DMVA Strategic Plan 2025-2029 | Goals, objectives, priority questions (`r nrow(load_priorities() |> filter(agency == "DMVA"))` rows) | [OSBM agency plans](https://www.osbm.nc.gov/operational-excellence/strategic-planning/agency-strategic-plans) |
| ACS 2023 5-year | County, state and congressional-district population counts (districts as drawn for the 118th Congress) | Census API |
| Census TIGER boundaries | County land area (for the rural / suburban / urban grouping) and map outlines | Census, via `tigris` |
| CDC PLACES | County health and social-need prevalence | CDC API |
| HRSA HPSA | Shortage-area designations | HRSA data warehouse |
| OpenFEMA | Disaster declarations since `r format(FEMA_DECLARATIONS_SINCE, "%Y")` | FEMA API |
| NCHS drug poisoning mortality | Model-based county death rates, `r min(OVERDOSE_YEARS)`-`r max(OVERDOSE_YEARS)` average | CDC open data (`rpvx-m2md`) |
| Capability profiles | 14 capabilities per agency, each with a control level and a source | Hand-built from public sources (`data/manual/agency_capabilities.csv`) |
| Local-model labels | Requirements, domain, plan alignment and evidence for `r n_fmt(nrow(label_set(grants)))` candidates | `qwen2.5:14b` via Ollama, cached |
| Team hand labels and reviews | 60 blind hand labels; review of 27 flagged research awards | `data/manual/handlabels_60.csv`, `spotcheck.csv` |

```{r plan-verify}
#| code-summary: "Check every plan row against its PDF page"
plan_check <- verify_priorities_against_pdf()
```

Every one of the `r nrow(plan_check)` strategic-plan rows is checked on each render: `r sum(plan_check$on_page)`
appear word-for-word on the PDF page they cite.

**What the strategic plans contain.** Each plan was turned into one row per goal, objective,
strategy and priority question. Rows about how the department runs itself (staffing, pay,
contracting, buildings) are marked *internal operations*; a federal program grant cannot align
with those, so they are left out of alignment scoring.

```{r plan-structure}
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| code-summary: "Strategic plan rows by goal"
load_priorities() |>
  mutate(goal = case_when(str_detect(priority_id, "^PQ") ~ "Priority questions",
                          !is.na(goal_id) ~ paste("Goal", str_remove(goal_id, "^G")),
                          TRUE ~ "Other"),
         kind = if_else(alignable, "Program work (scored)", "Internal operations (not scored)"),
         agency = paste(agency, if_else(agency == "DHHS", "2023-2025", "2025-2029"))) |>
  count(agency, goal, kind) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, fct_rev(goal), fill = kind)) +
  geom_col(width = .7, color = "white", linewidth = .3) +
  facet_wrap(~ agency, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Program work (scored)" = pal$blue, "Internal operations (not scored)" = "#C9D6E3"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "DMVA's plan is a third internal operations; DHHS's a quarter",
       subtitle = "Rows in each strategic plan table, by goal", x = "Plan rows", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
```

::: {.takeaway}
Only program rows can match a federal grant. Leaving internal-operations rows in let grant
boilerplate about staff and budgets look "aligned" (section 15).
:::

**What is missing from the structured data.** Counting opportunities whose text (title,
abstract, eligibility and description fields) mentions each requirement shows how little of a
go/no-go decision the export carries:

```{r missing-requirements}
#| code-summary: "Requirement mentions across all opportunities"
req_patterns <- c(
  "A specific match percentage"    = MATCH_PCT_PATTERN,
  "Non-federal share or match"     = "non-federal (share|match)",
  "In-kind contribution"           = "in-kind",
  "Letter of intent"               = "letters? of intent",
  "Letters of support/commitment"  = "letters? of (support|commitment)",
  "Evaluation plan"                = "evaluation plan",
  "Memorandum of understanding"    = "memorand(um|a) of understanding|\\bmou\\b",
  "Indirect cost terms"            = "indirect cost",
  "Subrecipients or subawards"     = "sub-?recipient|sub-?award")
tibble(requirement = names(req_patterns),
       opportunities = map_int(req_patterns, ~ sum(str_detect(grants$match_text, regex(.x, ignore_case = TRUE))))) |>
  dt(dom = "t")
```

**What kinds of funding are in the file.**

```{r funding-types}
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| code-summary: "Funding instruments and categories"
bind_rows(

  tibble(value = grants$category, panel = "Category")) |>
  mutate(value = str_replace_all(str_to_sentence(value), "_", " ")) |>

  ggplot(aes(n, reorder(value, n))) +
  geom_col(fill = pal$blue, width = .7) +

  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .28))) +
  labs(title = "Mostly discretionary grants and cooperative agreements",
       caption = NULL,
       subtitle = str_wrap("An opportunity can list more than one instrument. Cooperative agreements mean ongoing federal involvement and more staff time.", 85),
       x = "Opportunities", y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

::: {.takeaway}
Almost everything is discretionary, which means competitive: an application costs staff weeks
with no guarantee. About four in ten are cooperative agreements, where the federal agency stays
involved and reporting takes more staff time.
:::

# 5. Preprocessing

Every column is read as text and converted explicitly. Letting the reader guess types from the
first 1,000 rows silently turned `forecasted_close_date_description` into a logical column and
dropped `r sum(!is.na(grants_raw$forecasted_close_date_description))` values. Dates outside
`r format(DATE_MIN_VALID)` to `r format(DATE_MAX_VALID)` (including the 2099-01-01 sentinel)
are kept in `*_raw` columns and removed from analysis. HTML is stripped from abstracts.

```{r date-audit}
#| code-summary: "Date outlier audit"
tibble(
  check = c("Close date is the 2099-01-01 sentinel", "Posted rows with no close date",
            "Rows with any out-of-range date", "Close date before post date",
            "Closed in the 60 days before the pull date"),
  rows = c(sum(grants$close_date_raw >= as.Date("2099-01-01"), na.rm = TRUE),
           sum(grants$status_group == "Posted" & is.na(grants$close_date)),
           sum(grants$date_outlier_flag),
           sum(grants$close_date < grants$post_date, na.rm = TRUE),
           as.integer(fact_val("Rows closed in the 60 days before the pull date")))
) |> dt(dom = "t")
```

**Verified facts.** Before building anything we computed 24 facts directly from the file. The
pipeline must reproduce each one; the table below is recomputed on every render.

```{r facts-table}
#| code-summary: "Verified facts check"
facts |> dt(dom = "t", pageLength = 30)
```

`r sum(facts$result == "PASS")` of `r nrow(facts)` rows pass. One row was corrected during the
build: our original count of rows stating a match percentage was 1; the code found 6, all six
were checked by hand, and the fact was changed to 6.

# 6. The haystack

```{r funnel}
#| code-summary: "Funnel from the full file to the three piles"
dhhs_view <- keep(opps, ~ "DHHS" %in% unlist(.x$audience))
nonnih_open <- open_state |> filter(!is_nih)
relevant <- nonnih_open |> filter(opportunity_number %in% map_chr(dhhs_view, "number"),
  !map_lgl(opportunity_number, function(n) { o <- keep(opps, ~ .x$number == n)[[1]]
    s <- o$screen; isTRUE(s$is_research_mechanism) || isTRUE(s$is_restricted) || isTRUE(s$not_administrable) }))
funnel <- tibble(
  stage = c("All opportunities", "Posted (not forecast)", "State governments eligible",
            paste("Open through", format(cutoff_date, "%b %d")), "Not NIH research",
            "Relevant to DHHS and administrable", "In Tiers 1-3 (tool's opening scenario)"),
  n = c(nrow(grants), sum(grants$status_group == "Posted"),
        sum(grants$status_group == "Posted" & grants$state_eligible), nrow(open_state),
        nrow(nonnih_open), nrow(relevant), sum(opening$placement == "pile" & opening$tier <= 3))
) |> mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = rev(stage)))
ggplot(funnel, aes(n, stage)) +
  geom_col(fill = pal$blue, width = .7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_fmt(n)), hjust = -.15, size = 3.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .12))) +
  labs(title = "From 1,662 opportunities to the few a DHHS writer can act on",
       subtitle = str_wrap("Each stage keeps only rows that passed every earlier stage. The last stage is the tool's opening scenario, which also includes forecasts.", 95),
       x = "Opportunities", y = NULL)
```

The largest single drop is NIH. `r pct_fmt(mean(open_state$is_nih))` of open, state-eligible
opportunities are NIH research awards that expect a university investigator. Of the
`r nrow(nonnih_open)` that remain, most are not health and human services work at all:
economic development, outdoor recreation, traffic safety, agriculture, museums.
`r if (labels_ok) paste0("After the labeler's review, ", nrow(relevant), " are relevant to DHHS and administrable by a state agency.") else "The labeler's review of relevance is still running; this count updates when it finishes."`

The file also ages quickly: `r n_fmt(closed_since)` opportunities listed as posted in the
`r format(PULL_DATE, "%B %d")` export were closed or archived when we re-checked Grants.gov on
`r str_sub(na.omit(enrich$status$status_checked)[1], 1, 10)`.

```{r issuers}

grants |>

                            str_detect(agency_code, "^HHS") ~ paste0("HHS: ", str_remove(agency_name, " - .*$")),
                            TRUE ~ coalesce(top_level_agency_name, agency_name)),
```

# 7. Eligibility breadth

```{r breadth}
#| code-summary: "How many applicant types each opportunity lists"
ggplot(grants, aes(n_applicant_types)) +
  geom_bar(fill = pal$blue, width = .8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:16) +
  labs(title = "Eligibility is bimodal: one applicant type, or nearly all of them",
       subtitle = paste0(n_fmt(sum(grants$n_applicant_types == 1)), " rows list one type; ",
                         n_fmt(sum(grants$n_applicant_types == 15)), " list fifteen"),
       x = "Applicant types listed", y = "Opportunities")
```

`r n_fmt(nrow(state_rows))` rows list state governments. Only
`r sum(state_rows$state_only)` are restricted to state governments alone, and
`r sum(state_rows$n_applicant_types <= 3)` list three or fewer applicant types. For everything
else a state agency competes with universities, hospitals, nonprofits and companies.
Eligibility is a floor, not a signal of fit.

# 8. Deadline reality

```{r windows}
#| code-summary: "Application window distribution"
ggplot(windows, aes(application_window_days)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 7, fill = pal$blue, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = WINDOW_CUTOFFS_DAYS, linetype = "dashed", color = pal$red) +
  annotate("text", x = max(WINDOW_CUTOFFS_DAYS) + 6, y = Inf, vjust = c(1.6, 3.4), hjust = 0, color = pal$red, size = 3.4,
           label = paste0(WINDOW_CUTOFFS_DAYS, " days or fewer: ",
                          pct_fmt(c(mean(windows$application_window_days <= WINDOW_CUTOFFS_DAYS[1]),
                                    mean(windows$application_window_days <= WINDOW_CUTOFFS_DAYS[2])), 1))) +
  labs(title = "Most application windows are about two months",
       subtitle = paste0("Posted opportunities with a 0-", WINDOW_MAX_DAYS, " day window, n = ", n_fmt(nrow(windows))),
       x = "Days from posting to deadline", y = "Opportunities")
```

The median window is `r median(windows$application_window_days)` days; a quarter are
`r quantile(windows$application_window_days, .25, names = FALSE)` days or shorter and a tenth
`r quantile(windows$application_window_days, .10, names = FALSE)` or shorter. A writer who
learns of a posting three weeks late has lost a third of a typical window, which is why runway
is a user setting, not a fixed filter.

# 9. What an applicant actually receives

The file's `estimated_total_program_funding` is the national pot. Summed across open
state-eligible rows it reaches
`r usd_fmt(sum(open_state$estimated_total_program_funding, na.rm = TRUE))`, a number with no
meaning for one agency. We use the **implied per-award amount**: total funding divided by
expected awards, available for `r n_fmt(nrow(implied))` rows.

```{r implied}
#| code-summary: "Implied award vs stated ceiling"
cmp <- implied |> filter(!is.na(award_ceiling_clean))
ggplot(cmp, aes(award_ceiling_clean, implied_award_usd)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = pal$gray, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = .45, color = pal$blue, size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = usd_fmt, expand = expansion(mult = .05)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = usd_fmt, expand = expansion(mult = .06)) +
  labs(title = "The implied award tracks the stated ceiling",
       subtitle = paste0("n = ", n_fmt(nrow(cmp)), "; median implied / ceiling = ",
                         number(median(cmp$implied_award_usd / cmp$award_ceiling_clean), .01)),
       x = "Stated award ceiling (log)", y = "Implied award = total / expected awards (log)")
```

The median implied award is `r usd_fmt(median(implied$implied_award_usd))`. Where both exist,
the median ratio of implied award to stated ceiling is
`r number(median(cmp$implied_award_usd / cmp$award_ceiling_clean), .01)`, so the estimate
is consistent with what agencies say they will award. Where the implied value is missing, the
tool falls back to the ceiling and says so.

```{r award-distribution}
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| code-summary: "Distribution of the implied award"
ggplot(implied, aes(implied_award_usd)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = pal$blue, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(implied$implied_award_usd), linetype = "dashed", color = pal$red) +
  annotate("text", x = median(implied$implied_award_usd) * 1.3, y = Inf, vjust = 1.6, hjust = 0, color = pal$red, size = 3.4,
           label = paste("Median", usd_fmt(median(implied$implied_award_usd)))) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = usd_fmt) +
  labs(title = "What one award is worth: from thousands to tens of millions",
       subtitle = paste0("Implied award per recipient, n = ", n_fmt(nrow(implied)), " (log scale)"),
       x = "Implied award", y = "Opportunities")
```

::: {.takeaway}
Awards span four orders of magnitude, so a minimum-award setting matters: a $50K award rarely
justifies the same staff weeks as a $5M one.
:::

# 10. The capability model

Each agency has a hand-authored capability profile: fourteen capabilities, each with a control
level and a source. `direct` means the agency runs it; `contracted` means through a contract it
controls; `partner` means another entity controls it and an agreement is needed; `none` means
no route.

```{r capability-table}
#| code-summary: "Sourced capability profiles"
load_capabilities() |>
  mutate(source = sprintf('<a href="%s" target="_blank">source</a>', source_url)) |>
  select(agency, capability = capability_label, control = control_level, basis = notes,
         `what resolving a gap takes` = to_resolve, source) |>
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE, filter = "top", class = "cell-border stripe hover",
                options = list(pageLength = 14, scrollX = TRUE))
```

```{r capability-heatmap}
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| code-summary: "Capability profiles as a heatmap"
lvl <- c(direct = "Runs it directly", contracted = "Through a contract", partner = "Needs a partner", none = "No route")
load_capabilities() |>
  mutate(control = factor(lvl[control_level], levels = lvl),
         capability = fct_reorder(str_wrap(capability_label, 38), as.integer(factor(control_level, levels = names(lvl))), .fun = mean, .desc = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(agency, capability, fill = control)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = control), size = 3, color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Runs it directly" = "#0d366b", "Through a contract" = "#2a78d6",
                               "Needs a partner" = "#eb6834", "No route" = "#9a3412"), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(title = "What each agency controls, and where it needs someone else",
       subtitle = "Fourteen capabilities an opportunity can require; every cell is sourced in the table above",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
```

::: {.takeaway}
DHHS runs surveillance, labs, data systems and long-term care, and contracts clinical and
behavioral health services, but needs partners for housing, research, workforce training,
construction and emergency management. DMVA runs benefits eligibility and contracts its veterans
homes; almost everything else needs a partner or has no route. Every orange or red cell is a gap
that moves an opportunity to Tier 2 or Tier 3.
:::

Housing is the demonstration case. DHHS works on housing instability but does not control housing
stock; it reaches affordable units through the NC Housing Finance Agency's Targeting Program. So
housing is `partner`, and any opportunity that requires housing is at least Tier 2.

Each opportunity gets a requirement profile. For the `r n_fmt(nrow(label_set(grants)))`
candidates it comes from the local labeler (section 12), which reads the abstract and, for
`r n_fmt(nofo_n)` of them, the full announcement. For everything else it comes from
deterministic rules: the structured cost-share flag, the funding instrument, and sentence-level
patterns that ignore negated sentences ("funds may not be used for construction").

# 11. Authority tiering

The rules live in one file, `src/tool/tiering.js`. The notebook does not re-implement them: the
tables below come from running that file through V8.

- **Tier 3** if any of: cost share on an award at or above
  `r usd_fmt(APPROPRIATION_THRESHOLD_USD)` (a stated assumption, adjustable in the tool);
  cost share when the writer has no match authority; a capital construction project; a formal
  state designation; a required capability the agency has no route to.
- **Tier 2** if not Tier 3 and any of: a required capability reached only through a partner; cost
  share that needs supervisor approval; funding and monitoring subrecipients; a cooperative
  agreement with a required evaluation; more staff time than the writer has.
- **Tier 4, partner-led research**: research awards (and programs a state agency is unlikely to
  lead) get their own pile below the three authority tiers. A university, research institution or
  other partner would be the applicant; the agency's role is partner. Any other rules that fire are
  still listed on the card. The user can hide this pile.
- **Tier 1** otherwise.

Before tiering, an opportunity is set aside, visibly, if it is not relevant to the agency, is a
forecast, has closed, is NIH or a research mechanism, is judged not administrable by a state
agency, is restricted to named applicants, has less runway than the user needs, or is below the
minimum award.

**Ranking within a pile.** The piles answer *whose signature is needed*; they are never blended
with anything else. Within each pile the tool orders opportunities by an impact score whose weights
the user sets: fit with the strategic plan (the labeler's strong / partial / none), people reached,
help per person, award size, and the user's program priorities. The user can pick the one that
matters most or set each weight directly, and each card shows which parts led its score. Keeping
the score *inside* the piles is deliberate: a large award the agency cannot staff should not
outrank a small one it can run tomorrow, so authority is decided first and impact only orders what
remains.

```{r tier-table}
#| code-summary: "Tiers in the tool's opening scenario (computed by tiering.js)"
opening |> filter(placement == "pile", tier <= 3) |> arrange(tier) |>
  transmute(tier, opportunity = opportunity_title, agency = agency_code, reason = tier_reason) |>
  dt(pageLength = 15)
```

```{r tiers-by-scenario}
#| fig-height: 4
#| code-summary: "How the piles change with the writer's situation (tiering.js at each preset)"
scen <- map(payload$config$presets, ~ list(label = paste0(.x$label, if (.x$id == payload$config$opening_preset) " (opening)" else ""),
                                             settings = modifyList(payload$config$opening, .x$settings)))
map_dfr(scen, function(sc) {
  run_tiering_js(opps, payload$capabilities$profiles, sc$settings) |>
    filter(placement == "pile", tier <= 3) |> count(tier) |> mutate(scenario = sc$label)
}) |>
  mutate(tier = factor(paste("Tier", tier), levels = paste("Tier", 3:1)),
         scenario = factor(scenario, levels = rev(map_chr(scen, "label")))) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, scenario, fill = tier)) +
  geom_col(width = .65, color = "white", linewidth = .4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Tier 1" = pal$tier1, "Tier 2" = pal$tier2, "Tier 3" = pal$tier3), name = NULL,
                    breaks = paste("Tier", 1:3)) +
  labs(title = "Same opportunities, different piles",
       subtitle = str_wrap("Tiers 1-3 under each preset. The two presets that leave out forecasts have far fewer options; with no match authority (deadline crunch), nothing is left in Tier 1.", 90),
       x = "Opportunities in Tiers 1-3", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

::: {.takeaway}
The piles depend on the writer's situation. The same file gives a well-backed writer dozens of
options and a writer with no match authority almost none, which is why the tool asks first.
:::

```{r tiers-by-domain}
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| code-summary: "Program areas in the opening scenario's piles"
dom_of <- setNames(map_chr(opps, ~ .x$domain %||% NA_character_), map_chr(opps, "number"))
opening |> filter(placement == "pile", tier <= 3) |>
  mutate(domain = coalesce(unname(DOMAINS[dom_of[opportunity_number]]), "No domain assigned"),

  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Tier 1" = pal$tier1, "Tier 2" = pal$tier2, "Tier 3" = pal$tier3), name = NULL,
                    breaks = paste("Tier", 1:3)) +
  labs(title = "What DHHS can pursue now is mostly public health preparedness",
       subtitle = "Opening scenario, Tiers 1-3, by program domain", x = "Opportunities", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

::: {.takeaway}
Preparedness and infectious disease dominate what DHHS can pursue now, mostly through CDC
cooperative agreements with health departments. Other program areas depend on forecasts posting.

# 12. LLM labeling

**Method.** A local model (`r LLM_LABEL_MODEL`, run through Ollama; prompt `r LLM_PROMPT_VERSION`)
labels each candidate from its abstract plus a fixed excerpt of its full announcement: the first
`r n_fmt(LLM_NOFO_HEAD_CHARS)` characters, then sentences that mention match, subawards,
evaluation, construction, designation or renewal. Output must match a JSON schema with closed
vocabularies, at temperature 0 and a fixed seed, and evidence fields must quote the text.

**Caching.** Each response is stored under a SHA-256 hash of the model digest, prompt version,
and exact prompt. Rendering this notebook never calls the model; the labels below are read from
that cache.

```{r labeling-status}
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "Labeling coverage"
if (labels_ok) {
  cat(sprintf("Labeled: **%s of %s** candidates; **%s** had a full announcement. Median model time per opportunity: %s seconds.\n",
              n_fmt(sum(labels$labeled)), n_fmt(nrow(labels)), n_fmt(sum(labels$labeled & labels$has_nofo)),
              round(median(labels$llm_seconds, na.rm = TRUE))))
} else {
  cat('<div class="pending">Labeling has not finished; this section fills in when <code>data/processed/llm_labels.rds</code> exists.</div>')
}
```

**What the labeler could read.** A full announcement usually exists only once an opportunity
posts, so the model reads forecasts from their short abstracts alone.

```{r nofo-coverage}
#| fig-height: 3
#| code-summary: "Full-announcement coverage among candidates"
enrich$nofo |>
  left_join(select(grants, opportunity_number, status_group), by = "opportunity_number") |>
  mutate(read = if_else(!is.na(nofo_text), "Full announcement read", "Abstract only"),
         status_group = coalesce(status_group, "Other")) |>
  count(status_group, read) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, status_group, fill = read)) +
  geom_col(width = .6, color = "white", linewidth = .3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Full announcement read" = pal$blue, "Abstract only" = "#C9D6E3"), name = NULL) +
  labs(title = "Forecasts rarely have a full announcement yet",
       subtitle = paste0(n_fmt(nofo_n), " of ", n_fmt(cand_n), " candidates had a full announcement to read"),
       x = "Candidate opportunities", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

**How we tightened the labeler.** The first full prompt (v2) was reviewed after
`r if (file.exists(file.path(DIR_PROCESSED, "llm_labels_v2_partial.rds"))) nrow(readRDS(file.path(DIR_PROCESSED, "llm_labels_v2_partial.rds"))) else "some"`
labels, before any hand labels existed. It was too generous: it rated most opportunities at least
"partially" aligned with DHHS through generic objectives such as investing in partners' capacity,
put wildfire and international programs into the preparedness domain, and marked nearly
everything as something a state agency could run. Prompt v3 made the definitions strict (for
example, "a link that rests only on general words such as capacity, partners, equity or
disparities is none"; "work outside the United States is not administrable") and was checked on
twelve known cases before the full run. The same opportunities, labeled by both versions:

```{r prompt-iteration}
#| code-summary: "Prompt v2 vs v3 on the same opportunities"
v2_path <- file.path(DIR_PROCESSED, "llm_labels_v2_partial.rds")
if (labels_ok && file.exists(v2_path)) {
  v2 <- readRDS(v2_path) |> filter(labeled)
  both <- inner_join(v2, filter(labels, labeled), by = "opportunity_number", suffix = c("_v2", "_v3"))
  rate <- function(x) pct_fmt(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  tibble(
    measure = c("Rated at least partially aligned with DHHS", "Judged administrable by a state agency",
                "Placed in the preparedness / disaster domain (D08)", "Placed in no domain",
                "Formal evaluation required", "Match required (with a quoted source)"),
    `prompt v2` = c(rate(both$llm_align_dhhs_v2 %in% c("strong", "partial")), rate(both$llm_administrable_v2),
                    rate(both$llm_domain_v2 == "D08"), rate(both$llm_domain_v2 == "none"),
                    rate(both$llm_evaluation_v2), rate(both$llm_match_required_v2 %in% TRUE)),
    `prompt v3` = c(rate(both$llm_align_dhhs_v3 %in% c("strong", "partial")), rate(both$llm_administrable_v3),
                    rate(both$llm_domain_v3 == "D08"), rate(both$llm_domain_v3 == "none"),
                    rate(both$llm_evaluation_v3), rate(both$llm_match_required_v3))
  ) |> dt(dom = "t")
} else HTML('<div class="pending">Fills in when the v3 labels exist.</div>')
```

```{r prompt-iteration-examples}
#| code-summary: "Examples where v3 withdrew DHHS alignment"
if (labels_ok && file.exists(v2_path)) {
  both |> filter(llm_align_dhhs_v2 %in% c("strong", "partial"), llm_align_dhhs_v3 == "none") |>
    left_join(titles, by = "opportunity_number") |>
    transmute(opportunity = opportunity_title, agency = agency_code,
              `v2 alignment` = llm_align_dhhs_v2, `v2 reason` = llm_align_dhhs_why_v2,
              `v3 administrable` = llm_administrable_v3, `v3 domain` = llm_domain_v3) |>
    dt(pageLength = 8)
}
```

```{r prompt-iteration-chart}
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| code-summary: "Prompt v2 vs v3.1, chart"
if (labels_ok && file.exists(v2_path)) {
  tibble(measure = c("Aligned with DHHS (partial or strong)", "Administrable by a state agency", "Preparedness / disaster domain", "Formal evaluation required"),
         v2 = c(mean(both$llm_align_dhhs_v2 %in% c("strong", "partial")), mean(both$llm_administrable_v2), mean(both$llm_domain_v2 == "D08"), mean(both$llm_evaluation_v2)),
         v3 = c(mean(both$llm_align_dhhs_v3 %in% c("strong", "partial")), mean(both$llm_administrable_v3), mean(both$llm_domain_v3 == "D08"), mean(both$llm_evaluation_v3))) |>
    pivot_longer(c(v2, v3), names_to = "prompt", values_to = "share") |>
    mutate(prompt = if_else(prompt == "v2", "Prompt v2", "Prompt v3.1")) |>
    ggplot(aes(share, str_wrap(measure, 30), fill = prompt)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .75), width = .7) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Prompt v2" = "#C9D6E3", "Prompt v3.1" = pal$blue), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(title = "Tightening the prompt cut over-generous labels",
         subtitle = paste0("Same ", nrow(both), " opportunities labeled by both versions"), x = "Share of opportunities", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
```

::: {.takeaway}
The first prompt said "yes" too easily. Making the definitions strict cut the share called
"aligned with DHHS" by about two-thirds, mostly by removing wildfire, international and
research programs.
:::

**What the labeler found.** Across all labeled candidates, the capabilities it most often said an
opportunity requires, and the DHHS plan rows it most often cited as the link:

```{r label-capabilities}
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| code-summary: "Capabilities the labeler found"
if (labels_ok) {
  cap_lab <- setNames(map_chr(payload$capabilities$vocab, "label"), map_chr(payload$capabilities$vocab, "id"))
  tibble(cap = unlist(filter(labels, labeled)$llm_capabilities)) |>
    count(cap) |>
    mutate(cap = coalesce(cap_lab[cap], cap)) |>
    ggplot(aes(n, fct_reorder(cap, n))) +
    geom_col(fill = pal$blue, width = .7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -.3, size = 3.3) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .1))) +
    labs(title = "Surveillance and data systems are the most common requirements",
         subtitle = paste0("Required capabilities found in ", sum(labels$labeled), " labeled candidates (an opportunity can need several)"),
         x = "Opportunities", y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
```

```{r label-plan-rows}
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| code-summary: "DHHS plan rows the labeler cited"
if (labels_ok) {
  pr_txt <- load_priorities() |> filter(agency == "DHHS") |> select(priority_id, text)
  filter(labels, labeled, llm_align_dhhs %in% c("strong", "partial"), !is.na(llm_align_dhhs_row), llm_align_dhhs_row != "none") |>
    count(priority_id = llm_align_dhhs_row, level = str_to_sentence(llm_align_dhhs)) |>
    left_join(pr_txt, by = "priority_id") |>
    group_by(priority_id) |> mutate(total = sum(n)) |> ungroup() |>
    filter(dense_rank(desc(total)) <= 10) |>
    mutate(row = fct_reorder(str_wrap(paste0(priority_id, ": ", str_trunc(coalesce(text, ""), 70)), 55), total),
           level = factor(level, levels = c("Partial", "Strong"))) |>
    ggplot(aes(n, row, fill = level)) +
    geom_col(width = .7, color = "white", linewidth = .3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Strong" = pal$blue, "Partial" = "#9DBFE3"), name = "Alignment") +
    labs(title = "The plan rows opportunities connect to",
         subtitle = "Ten DHHS plan rows most often cited as the link, among opportunities rated aligned",
         x = "Opportunities citing the row", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8.5))
}
```

::: {.takeaway}
The two most common requirements, surveillance and data systems, are ones DHHS runs directly.
The third, research capacity, is one it reaches only through universities, which is what defines
Tier 4.
:::

Two caveats. The v2 labels were scored against DHHS's 2024-2026 plan before we switched to the
plan the competition provides, so plan-row citations differ between versions; the alignment
*levels* are still comparable. And v3 still misses some research networks that do not use
activity codes like R01; the hand-label comparison below measures how often.

**The prompt.** The full labeling prompt is generated by `prompt_prefix()` and `build_prompt()`
in `src/R/03_llm_label.R`; the text below is produced from that code on every render, so it is
exactly what the model received. The fixed part (instructions, definitions, both strategic plans)
comes first; the opportunity's own text is appended at the end.

```{r show-prompt}
#| code-summary: "Print the prompt and the output schema"
#| class-output: "prompt-text"
pr_align <- alignable_priorities()
example <- label_set(grants) |> filter(opportunity_number == "PA-FPH-27-001")
example_nofo <- enrich$nofo$nofo_text[enrich$nofo$opportunity_number == "PA-FPH-27-001"]
prompt_text <- build_prompt(example, nofo_excerpt(if (length(example_nofo)) example_nofo else NA_character_), pr_align)
cat(str_trunc(prompt_text, 9000, side = "center", ellipsis = "\n[... middle of the example opportunity's text omitted here ...]\n"))
```

<details><summary>Output schema the model must match (JSON Schema)</summary>

```{r show-schema}
#| echo: false
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(label_schema(pr_align), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE))
```

</details>

**Validation against hand labels.** Sixty candidates were drawn at random, stratified by
status, issuing agency family, and whether a full announcement exists, and labeled by team
members who had not seen the model's answers.

```{r validation}
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "Accuracy, precision and recall"
if (is.null(validation)) {
  cat('<div class="pending">Waiting for <code>data/manual/handlabels_60.csv</code>. The comparison runs automatically once it exists.</div>')
} else {
  print(htmltools::tagList(
    dt(validation$summary |> mutate(accuracy = pct_fmt(accuracy)), dom = "t", pageLength = 20),
    dt(validation$capabilities |> mutate(across(c(precision, recall), pct_fmt)), dom = "t"),
    dt(validation$by_class |> mutate(across(c(precision, recall), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "n/a", pct_fmt(.x)))), pageLength = 15)
  ))
}
```

```{r accuracy-dots}
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| code-summary: "Agreement with the team, by field"
if (!is.null(validation)) {
  facts_f <- c("match required", "capital project", "designation")
  validation$summary |> filter(!is.na(accuracy)) |>
    mutate(kind = if_else(field %in% facts_f, "Stated fact", "Judgment call"),
           field = str_replace_all(str_to_sentence(field), c("Dmva" = "DMVA", "Dhhs" = "DHHS")),
           field = fct_reorder(paste0(field, "  (n = ", n, ")"), accuracy)) |>
    ggplot(aes(accuracy, field, color = kind)) +
    geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = accuracy, yend = field), linewidth = .8, alpha = .5) +
    geom_point(size = 3.4) +
    geom_text(aes(label = pct_fmt(accuracy)), hjust = -.45, size = 3.4, color = pal$dark) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Stated fact" = pal$blue, "Judgment call" = pal$orange), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1.08), breaks = seq(0, 1, .25)) +
    labs(title = "Reliable on stated facts, weaker on judgment",
         subtitle = "Share of the team's blind hand labels the model matched",
         x = "Agreement", y = NULL) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
```

::: {.takeaway}
The facts that put an opportunity in Tier 3 (match, construction, designation) agree over 90% of
the time. Judgment calls (could a state lead it, how well it fits the plan) agree about half to
two-thirds of the time, so the tool shows the model's evidence on every card. DMVA alignment scores
high only because almost nothing in the file concerns veterans, so "none" is usually right.
:::

```{r confusion-heatmaps}
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| code-summary: "Where the model and the team disagree"
if (!is.null(validation)) {
  map_dfr(c("administrable", "DHHS alignment"), function(f) {
    as.data.frame(validation$confusion[[f]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
      mutate(field = if (f == "administrable") "Administrable by a state agency" else "DHHS alignment")
  }) |>
    mutate(across(c(human, model), ~ str_to_sentence(.x))) |>
    group_by(field) |> mutate(share = Freq / sum(Freq)) |> ungroup() |>
    ggplot(aes(model, human, fill = Freq)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(aes(label = Freq, color = Freq > max(Freq) / 2), size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = pal$dark)) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#EEF4FA", high = pal$blue, guide = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~ field, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = "Where the model and the team disagree",
         subtitle = "Rows: team's hand label. Columns: model. The diagonal is agreement.", x = "Model", y = "Team") +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))
}
```

```{r error-examples}
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "Where the model disagreed with the humans"
if (!is.null(validation) && nrow(validation$disagreements) > 0) {
  hl_notes <- handlabels |> select(opportunity_number, team_notes = notes)
  validation$disagreements |>
    filter(field %in% c("administrable", "DHHS alignment", "match required", "domain")) |>
    left_join(select(grants, opportunity_number, opportunity_title, summary_text), by = "opportunity_number") |>
    left_join(select(labels, opportunity_number, llm_administrable_evidence, llm_align_dhhs_why, llm_match_evidence), by = "opportunity_number") |>
    left_join(hl_notes, by = "opportunity_number") |>
    transmute(field, opportunity = opportunity_title, team = human, model,
              `model's own evidence or reason` = case_when(
                field == "administrable" ~ llm_administrable_evidence,
                field == "DHHS alignment" ~ llm_align_dhhs_why,
                field == "match required" ~ llm_match_evidence, TRUE ~ ""),
              `team notes` = coalesce(team_notes, ""),
              abstract = str_trunc(summary_text, 350)) |>
    dt(pageLength = 6) |> print()
} else {
  cat('<div class="pending">Disagreement examples appear here once hand labels exist. We quote real errors only.</div>')
}
```

```{r validation-caveats}
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "Caveats on the comparison"
if (!is.null(validation)) {
  dev <- readr::read_csv(file.path(DIR_MANUAL, "prompt_dev_cases.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  dev_ids <- grants$opportunity_number[map_lgl(grants$opportunity_title, function(t) any(str_detect(t, fixed(dev$title_contains))))]
  overlap <- intersect(dev_ids, handlabels$opportunity_number)
  cat(sprintf("- **Tuning overlap.** Prompt v3.1 was checked against %d development cases chosen before the hand labels existed. %d of them are also in the 60-row hand-label sample%s. Their agreement could be slightly flattering; the rest of the sample was never used for tuning.\n",
              nrow(dev), length(overlap), if (length(overlap)) paste0(" (", paste(overlap, collapse = ", "), ")") else ""))
  if (length(validation$not_comparable))
    cat(sprintf("- **Not comparable:** %s. The team described these in free text rather than choosing from the model's fixed categories, so agreement cannot be scored automatically.\n",
                paste(validation$not_comparable, collapse = ", ")))
  if (nrow(validation$out_of_taxonomy))
    cat(sprintf("- **Outside the taxonomy:** %d hand labels use a domain that is not one of the eight (%s). The model cannot choose it, so these count as disagreements.\n",
                nrow(validation$out_of_taxonomy), paste(unique(validation$out_of_taxonomy$human), collapse = "; ")))
}
```

```{r match-disagreements}
#| results: asis
#| code-summary: "Check the match disagreements against the source text"
if (!is.null(validation)) {
  md <- validation$disagreements |> filter(field == "match required") |>
    left_join(select(grants, opportunity_number, is_cost_sharing, summary_text), by = "opportunity_number") |>
    left_join(select(labels, opportunity_number, llm_match_evidence), by = "opportunity_number") |>
    left_join(select(enrich$nofo, opportunity_number, nofo_text), by = "opportunity_number") |>
    mutate(quote_in_text = map2_lgl(llm_match_evidence, paste(summary_text, coalesce(nofo_text, "")), function(ev, hay)
             nzchar(coalesce(ev, "")) && str_detect(str_squish(str_to_lower(hay)), fixed(str_sub(str_squish(str_to_lower(ev)), 1, 60)))))
  backed <- sum(md$model == "TRUE" & md$is_cost_sharing & md$quote_in_text)
  cat(sprintf("**Not every disagreement is a model error.** Of the %d disagreements on whether match is required, %d have the model saying *required* where the structured data's own cost-sharing flag also says required and the model's quote appears word for word in the announcement (for example: \"%s\"). Those are hand-label slips, not model errors; we report the raw agreement and leave the team's labels as written.\n",
              nrow(md), backed, if (backed) md$llm_match_evidence[which(md$model == "TRUE" & md$is_cost_sharing & md$quote_in_text)[1]] else ""))
}
```
